messages:
alex_pm: Quick sync — Q4 planning for private delivery: need a decision on control-plane placement, packaging format for on-prem customers, and an approach for air-gapped installs. Customers pushing timelines; want a recommended proposal by EOW.
jonah_eng: +1. Do we have a preferred starting point? VPC-hosted control plane (we manage CP but customer VPC peering) vs customer-hosted CP (customers run control plane)?
maya_sec: Security checklist: if we host CP in our infra, customers need clear IAM boundaries, audit logs export, and optional KMS passthrough. Airgap adds signing + offline license activation.
alex_pm: My tilt: start with a "managed control plane in tenant VPC" pattern — less ops on customers and faster time-to-value. But branch to a customer-hosted path for high-regulation accounts. Need cost/ops tradeoffs from eng.
jonah_eng: Engineering estimates: managed-in-VPC (peer+private-route) is ~3w infra work + infra-as-code templates + testing. Customer-hosted CP is ~6-8w (multi-tenant isolation, install UX). On-prem packaging (deb/rpm + tarball) adds ~2w per distro family.
sam_solutions: From sales/solutions feedback: most early enterprise pilots prefer we handle control plane but insist on private network peering and customer-managed keys. They ask for an installer that doesn't require continuous internet for runtime.
linda_csm: Current list of customers asking: FinX (SaaS bank), HealthCo, GovLab — GovLab will absolutely require airgap. FinX wants rotation of keys via their KMS.
maya_sec: For airgap we need: signed release artifacts, offline bundle with checksums, offline activation token (time-limited), and HSM/KMS integration docs. Also a threat model update.
jonah_eng: Proposal draft for EOW:
```
Option A: Managed CP in customer VPC (fastest)
- Pros: quicker pilot, central ops, easier updates
- Cons: customers want KMS passthrough + strict egress rules
Estimated: 3w infra + 1w docs

Option B: Customer-hosted CP (self-managed)
- Pros: full customer control, fits airgap needs better
- Cons: heavier install, support burden
Estimated: 6-8w + packaging
```
alex_pm: Good. Let's map to OKRs: Objective: Make private deployments GA-ready. Key results: 1) Support 3 enterprise pilots with managed CP in VPC by EOY; 2) Deliver airgap installer + docs for 2 customers; 3) <10% increase in ops tickets month 1 post-deploy.
sam_solutions: Can we include a fallback plan: auto-fallback to hosted model if customer wants quick demo?
jonah_eng: We'll add a canary rollout plan and an emergency rollback. Also autoscale knobs to avoid capacity surprises.
maya_sec: Add compliance checklist for customers with FedRAMP/PCI notes. I'll draft the section.
linda_csm: I'll consolidate customer ask list and owners, and flag which ones require on-prem or airgap.
alex_pm: Action items: jonah to produce rough infra plan + effort estimate (due Wed), maya to produce security checklist (Thu), linda to hand over prioritized customer list (Thu), sam to prepare sales-facing pitch for managed CP (Thu). I'll synthesize into a proposal for exec review Fri.
deploy-bot: Reminder: #deployments schedule open for 2026-11-02 maintenance window.
jonah_eng: One more note: packaging artifacts should include a minimal systemd unit, offline license tool, and an example `values.yaml` for helm-free installs.
alex_pm: Thanks — short sync tomorrow 2pm to finalize wording. :thumbsup:
